_comment: The pre-filter that decides whether a message may leave this box.
It is a privacy control, not a cost control: mail from a sender that is
not listed here is never sent to a third party, whatever it says.
A missed booking is an inconvenience -- you add the hotel by hand. A
personal email sent to an API is not recoverable. The list is biased
accordingly, and is meant to be extended as new senders show up.
_confirmation_comment: Checked against subject and body. An allowed sender still has to look
like a booking -- their marketing mail should stay on the box too.
_deny_comment: Subject only. Real confirmations carry an unsubscribe footer in the body,
so matching denials against the body would veto the mail we want.
_immigration_comment: never unioned with allow_sender_domains above -- a government/immigration
sender must never ride in on 'looks like a hotel confirmation' logic, and
a hotel confirmation must never ride in on this list either. Every message
flagged here still stays on the box: services.immigration only matches it
to a trip and proposes a confirmation locally, it is never sent to the
extractor automatically (decision 4). Mapped to the country the sender
belongs to, so matching can prefer a same-country trip; an empty string
means 'recognised government sender, country not modelled yet'. Meant to
be extended as new senders show up, same as the travel allow-list.
_immigration_keyword_comment: Checked against subject and body, same as confirmation_keywords -- but a
disjoint list. 'Confirmed' alone should not flag a government email, and
'arrival card' alone should not flag a hotel one.
